# Kicker: the bot language

Kicker is a small, rule-based language for writing poker bots. There is no
machine learning and nothing hidden: your bot does exactly what its rules say.

```kicker
on preflop
  when hand in "TT+, AQs+, AKo" then raise 3 x     # premium hand: raise
  when top(20) and to_call <= 3 * bb then call      # decent hand, cheap: call
  check                                             # otherwise check, or fold to a bet
end

on postflop
  when strength > 0.8 then bet 75% pot              # very strong: bet for value
  when equity > pot_odds then call                  # the price is right: call
  check
end
```

## How a bot runs

Every time it is your bot's turn, the program runs **from top to bottom,
once**. The **first action** it reaches is the move. If it reaches none, the
bot checks when that is free and folds otherwise.

There are no loops and no user-defined functions, so every program finishes
instantly. A bot cannot touch the web page, the network or your computer, which
is why it is safe to run a friend's bot at your table.

## Actions

| Write | Does |
|---|---|
| `fold` | Folds. If checking is free, checks instead (folding for free is never right). |
| `check` | Checks; if someone has bet, folds. |
| `call` | Calls; if nothing to call, checks. |
| `allin` | Puts every chip in (or calls, if raising is not allowed). |
| `raise <size>` / `bet <size>` | Bets or raises. `bet` and `raise` mean the same thing. |

Raise sizes (always made legal for you: too small becomes the minimum raise,
too big becomes all-in, and if raising is not allowed it becomes a call):

| Size | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `raise 3 bb` | Raise to 3 big blinds. |
| `raise 2.5 x` | Raise to 2.5 times the current bet (or 2.5 big blinds if nobody bet). |
| `bet 75% pot` or `bet 0.75 pot` | A pot-sized raise scaled by 0.75: call first, then add 0.75 × the pot. |
| `bet pot` | A full pot-sized bet or raise. |
| `raise to 600` or `raise 600` | Make your total bet this round 600 chips. |
| `raise min` / `raise max` | Minimum raise / all-in. A bare `raise` is a minimum raise. |

Sizes can be expressions: `raise 2.5 + limpers bb`, `raise min(4, stack_bb) bb`.

## Conditions

```kicker
when strength > 0.8 then raise pot          # one statement, if true

if pocket_pair and stack_bb > 30 then       # blocks
  call
elif top(10)
  raise 3 x
else
  fold
end

on flop, turn                               # only on these streets
  when draw then call
end
```

`on` accepts `preflop`, `flop`, `turn`, `river` and `postflop` (flop,
turn or river), separated by commas. `then` is optional after `if` / `elif`.

## Values and operators

- Numbers: `3`, `0.75`, `75%` (the same as 0.75)
- Text: `"AKs"`, `'flop'`
- Yes/no: `true`, `false`
- Lists: `[1, 2, 3]`
- Arithmetic: `+ - * /` (dividing by zero gives 0). `+` also joins text.
- Comparisons: `== != < <= > >=`. They chain: `0.3 < equity < 0.6`.
- Logic: `and`, `or`, `not`
- Membership: `x in [1, 2]`, `hand in "TT+"`, `hand not in "Kx"`

## Hand ranges

Compare your starting hand to a range with `in`:

| Range | Means |
|---|---|
| `AA` | Pocket aces |
| `TT+` | Tens or better |
| `22-66` | Twos through sixes |
| `AKs` / `AKo` / `AK` | Suited / offsuit / either |
| `ATs+` | ATs, AJs, AQs, AKs |
| `A5s-A2s` | A5s, A4s, A3s, A2s |
| `87s-54s` | 87s, 76s, 65s, 54s |
| `Axs` / `Kx` | Any suited ace / any king |

Separate parts with commas: `hand in "TT+, AQs+, KQs, 76s-54s"`.

## Variables

```kicker
let price = to_call / bb        # for this decision only
keep bluffs = 0                 # remembered between hands (set the first time only)
when chance(0.1) then bluffs = bluffs + 1
```

Built-in names (below) cannot be reassigned. Misspelled names are caught when
you type them, with a "did you mean" hint.

## Talking and debugging

- `say "text"` shows a speech bubble at the table (and in the hand log).
- `log value` prints in the Bot Lab's **Try a spot** panel.

## About your bot

Optional lines at the top of the file:

```kicker
bot "Night Owl"
avatar "🦉"
color "#7dd3fc"
desc "Patient, then pounces."
author "you"
```

## Built-in reference

`equity` and `strength` come from dealing out hundreds of random hands
(Monte Carlo); before the flop they come from a precomputed table of all 169
starting hands. Opponents are assumed to hold random cards, so treat these as
a guide: a player who raises three times is not holding a random hand.

### Your cards

What you were dealt.

| Name | Type | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hand` | text | `"AKs"` | Your starting hand in poker notation: "AA", "AKs" (suited), "T9o" (offsuit). Check it against a range with `hand in "TT+, AQs+"`. |
| `high` | number | `14` | Rank of your higher card: 2..10, J = 11, Q = 12, K = 13, A = 14. |
| `low` | number | `9` | Rank of your lower card (same scale as `high`). |
| `suited` | yes/no | `true` | Both your cards are the same suit. |
| `pocket_pair` | yes/no | `false` | Your two cards are the same rank. |
| `connected` | yes/no | `true` | Your cards are next to each other in rank (98, JT, and A2 counts). |
| `gap` | number | `1` | Ranks missing between your cards: 0 for connectors (98), 1 for one-gappers (97). -1 for a pocket pair. |
| `top_pct` | number | `4.5` | How good your starting hand is: the percent of all hands at least this strong. AA = 0.45, AKs = 3, 72o = 99. Smaller is better. See also `top(n)`. |
| `chen` | number | `10` | Bill Chen's starting-hand score, from -1 (72o) to 20 (AA). |

### Board & made hand

What the community cards do for you. Before the flop most of these are false / 0.

| Name | Type | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `board_cards` | number | `3` | Number of community cards: 0, 3, 4 or 5. |
| `made` | text | `"two pair"` | Your best hand: "high card", "pair", "two pair", "trips", "straight", "flush", "full house", "quads" or "straight flush". |
| `made_rank` | number | `2` | Your best hand as a number: 0 high card, 1 pair, 2 two pair, 3 trips, 4 straight, 5 flush, 6 full house, 7 quads, 8 straight flush. |
| `board_rank` | number | `1` | The same scale for the board on its own (1 means the board is paired). |
| `hit` | yes/no | `true` | Your cards make your hand better than the board alone (made_rank > board_rank). Before the flop: you have a pocket pair. |
| `top_pair` | yes/no | `true` | One of your cards pairs the highest card on the board. |
| `overpair` | yes/no | `false` | You have a pocket pair higher than every board card. |
| `flush_draw` | yes/no | `false` | Four cards to a flush, using at least one of yours (flop or turn only). |
| `straight_draw` | yes/no | `false` | Open-ended straight draw (two ranks complete it) using your cards. |
| `gutshot` | yes/no | `false` | Inside straight draw (exactly one rank completes it). |
| `draw` | yes/no | `false` | `flush_draw or straight_draw`. |
| `outs` | number | `9` | Rough number of cards that complete your draws. |
| `board_paired` | yes/no | `false` | Two or more board cards share a rank. |
| `board_flushy` | yes/no | `false` | Three or more board cards share a suit, so a flush is possible. |
| `board_connected` | yes/no | `false` | Three board cards fit inside a five-rank window, so a straight is possible. |
| `board_high` | number | `13` | Highest board card rank (2..14), 0 before the flop. |

### Strength

Win chances, estimated by dealing out thousands of random hands.

| Name | Type | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `equity` | number | `0.62` | Chance to win (0..1) against every opponent still in the hand, assuming they hold random cards. Ties count as part-wins. |
| `strength` | number | `0.71` | Chance to win (0..1) against ONE random hand. Steadier than `equity` when many players are in: AA = 0.85, 72o = 0.35. |

### Chips & bets

All amounts are in chips unless the name ends in _bb (big blinds).

| Name | Type | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pot` | number | `450` | All chips in the pot, including bets in front of players this round. |
| `to_call` | number | `100` | Chips you need to put in to call (0 when you can check). |
| `stack` | number | `2400` | Chips you have behind (not counting what you already bet). |
| `bb` | number | `20` | The big blind. |
| `sb` | number | `10` | The small blind. |
| `ante` | number | `0` | The ante (tournaments, later levels). |
| `stack_bb` | number | `120` | Your stack in big blinds. |
| `pot_odds` | number | `0.25` | to_call / (pot + to_call): the share of the final pot you are paying. Calling is profitable when your equity is higher. |
| `spr` | number | `4.2` | Stack-to-pot ratio: stack / pot. |
| `current_bet` | number | `200` | The bet everyone has to match this round. |
| `my_bet` | number | `20` | What you already put in this round. |
| `invested` | number | `60` | What you put in this whole hand. |
| `min_raise` | number | `400` | Smallest legal raise, as the total you would raise to. |
| `max_raise` | number | `2420` | Largest raise (all-in), as a total. |
| `effective_stack` | number | `1800` | The smaller of your stack and the biggest opponent stack still in the hand: the most you can win or lose. |
| `effective_bb` | number | `90` | `effective_stack` in big blinds. |
| `can_check` | yes/no | `true` | Checking is free (nobody has bet). |
| `can_raise` | yes/no | `true` | You are allowed to raise (false when everyone else is all-in, for example). |
| `facing_bet` | yes/no | `false` | Someone bet and you must call, raise or fold. |

### Position & action

Where you sit and what happened so far.

| Name | Type | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `street` | text | `"flop"` | Current round: "preflop", "flop", "turn" or "river". |
| `preflop` | yes/no | `false` | It is before the flop. |
| `flop` | yes/no | `true` | It is the flop. |
| `turn` | yes/no | `false` | It is the turn. |
| `river` | yes/no | `false` | It is the river. |
| `postflop` | yes/no | `true` | Flop, turn or river. |
| `players` | number | `6` | Players dealt into this hand. |
| `active` | number | `3` | Players still in the hand (not folded), you included. |
| `opponents` | number | `2` | Opponents still in the hand. |
| `position` | number | `0.8` | Your seat relative to the button: 0 = first to act after the flop (small blind), 1 = the button (acts last). |
| `in_position` | yes/no | `true` | You act last after the flop among players still in. |
| `on_button` | yes/no | `false` | You are the dealer. |
| `in_blinds` | yes/no | `false` | You posted the small or big blind this hand. |
| `is_sb` | yes/no | `false` | You are the small blind. |
| `is_bb` | yes/no | `false` | You are the big blind. |
| `behind` | number | `2` | Players still to act after you this round who could still bet (not folded or all-in). |
| `raises` | number | `1` | Bets and raises made this round so far (blinds do not count). |
| `limpers` | number | `0` | Before the flop: players who just called the big blind before anyone raised. |
| `callers` | number | `1` | Players who called the latest bet or raise this round. |
| `aggressor` | yes/no | `false` | You made the latest bet or raise this round. |
| `was_aggressor` | yes/no | `true` | You made the last bet or raise of the previous round (e.g. you raised preflop: a continuation bet spot). |
| `first_action` | yes/no | `true` | This is your first decision of the hand. |
| `hand_number` | number | `57` | Hands played at this table so far. |

### Opponents

Averages over the opponents still in the hand, learned from what they did in earlier hands. They start near typical values (vpip 0.30, pfr 0.15, aggr 1.5) and move toward what each player really does.

| Name | Type | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `opp_vpip` | number | `0.30` | How often they put money in before the flop by choice (0..1). High = loose. |
| `opp_pfr` | number | `0.15` | How often they raise before the flop (0..1). |
| `opp_aggr` | number | `1.5` | Aggression: (bets + raises) / calls. Above 2 is aggressive, below 1 is passive. |
| `opp_hands` | number | `40` | Fewest hands seen of any opponent still in (how much to trust the stats). |

### Tournament

Zero / false outside tournaments.

| Name | Type | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tournament` | yes/no | `false` | You are playing a tournament. |
| `players_left` | number | `0` | Players still in the tournament. |
| `level` | number | `0` | Blind level (1 = first). |

### Functions

Call these with parentheses.

| Function | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `top(pct)` | True when your starting hand is in the best `pct` percent of hands. `top(10)` is roughly 88+, ATs+, KQs, AJo+. |
| `random()` | A random number from 0 up to (not including) 1. |
| `chance(p)` | True with probability p. `chance(0.3)` is true about 30% of the time. Use it to mix up your play. |
| `pick(a, b, ...)` | One of the values, chosen at random. Great for `say pick("Nice hand", "Lucky!")`. |
| `min(a, b, ...)` | The smallest value. |
| `max(a, b, ...)` | The largest value. |
| `abs(x)` | Absolute value. |
| `round(x, digits)` | Round to the nearest whole number, or to `digits` decimal places. |
| `floor(x)` | Round down. |
| `ceil(x)` | Round up. |
| `clamp(x, lo, hi)` | x, kept between lo and hi. |
| `between(x, lo, hi)` | True when lo <= x <= hi. Same as `lo <= x <= hi`. |
| `mod(a, b)` | Remainder of a / b (0 if b is 0). `mod(hand_number, 10) == 0` is true every tenth hand. |
| `in_range(hand, range)` | Same as `hand in range`: is the hand class in a range like "TT+, AQs+, KQs"? |
| `equity_vs(n)` | Chance to win against exactly n random hands (1..8), whoever is still in. |

## A complete example

This is the built-in **Shark**:

```kicker
bot "Shark"
avatar "🦈"
color "#38d6ff"
desc "Tight-aggressive pro. Position-aware opening ranges, bets strong hands for value, folds when beaten."

# How wide to open depends on the seat: tight up front, loose on the button.
let open = 10
if position >= 0.85 then
  open = 26
elif position >= 0.6 then
  open = 18
elif position >= 0.35 then
  open = 13
end

on preflop
  if raises == 0 then
    when top(open) then raise 2.5 + limpers bb
    when is_sb and behind == 1 and top(35) then raise 3 bb    # steal the big blind
    when can_check then check
    when limpers > 0 and in_position and top(open + 10) then call
    fold
  elif raises == 1 then
    when top(3) then raise 3 x                                 # 3-bet the best hands
    when top(open / 2) and pot_odds < 0.35 then call
    when pocket_pair and effective_bb > 25 and to_call < stack * 0.1 then call   # set mining
    fold
  else
    when top(1.5) then allin
    when top(3) and pot_odds < 0.4 then call
    fold
  end
end

on postflop
  # Players who keep betting usually have something: trust equity less.
  let eq = equity - 0.04 * raises
  if can_check then
    when eq > 0.75 then bet 0.75 pot
    when eq > 0.55 and opponents <= 2 then bet 0.6 pot
    when was_aggressor and opponents == 1 and chance(0.65) then bet 0.5 pot   # continuation bet
    when draw and chance(0.35) then bet 0.55 pot                               # semi-bluff
    check
  else
    when eq > 0.85 then raise 2.5 x
    when draw and can_raise and eq > pot_odds and chance(0.3) then raise 2.5 x
    when eq > pot_odds + 0.05 then call
    fold
  end
end
```

## Errors

- **Problems** (typos, a missing `end`, `=` instead of `==`) are shown as you
  type, with the line and a hint. A bot with problems cannot sit at a table.
- **Runtime errors** (say, comparing text with `<`) cannot crash anything:
  the bot checks or folds for that decision and the error appears in the hand
  log and the Bot Lab tester.
